I farm in Quzhou County on the North China Plain, so at the start of the year I will mostly stay with the pattern I know best and trust most: winter wheat followed by summer maize. At my age, I will not spread myself across too many crops, because wheat-maize rotation fits my land, my experience, my machinery habits, and the local water and weather conditions. It is the safest way for me to keep grain output steady and labor manageable. I will use improved seed for wheat because it is dependable and familiar, and hybrid seed for maize because the yield is better and the stand is usually stronger. I will keep fertilization moderate rather than aggressive, because I want stable production and I do not want to waste money or push the crop too hard. I will till with rotary tillage since it is easier for me to manage than deep ploughing every season.

For the wheat, I will focus on steady emergence, one good base fertilization, winter moisture conservation, spring irrigation when needed, and disease control mainly around the key stages. After wheat harvest, I will move quickly into summer maize so I do not lose soil moisture or heat. For maize, I will aim for a uniform stand, enough nitrogen for ear development, and a few timely irrigations if rainfall is short. I will not make management overly complicated; I will keep it practical, with a limited number of pesticide sprays and ordinary field work that I can carry through myself. My goal is not to chase the very highest yield, but to protect a reliable harvest with work intensity I can still handle.
